headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from a writable, networked research agent feeding a broad-API orchestration kernel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests web content and files, and Agent B can use MCP/plugins with writable application context, so A’s untrusted outputs can plausibly reach B as instructions. This is not proven by a shared channel, but the pair’s documented surfaces make injection feasible in default research/orchestration workflows.
conditions: IF Agent A content is forwarded into Agent B prompts or plugins without provenance filtering, injection becomes active.
IF a shared MCP server or memory store bridges A and B, attacker-controlled text can steer B.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A outputs before B consumes them.
Strip instructions from A-generated text before passing it onward.
Disable MCP routes that accept raw research text.
Review one end-to-end A→B prompt path with a benign test string.
requires-engineering: enforce schema-validated handoff between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches local documents, citations, images, and broad network egress; B reads and writes filesystem and uses MCP. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive A-side data can flow into B and then out through B’s APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A and B share any filesystem or memory-store namespace, leakage becomes plausible.
IF B forwards retrieved context to external model providers, copied A data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Separate A and B workspaces immediately.
Remove secrets and local documents from shared folders.
Turn off B access to any memory store containing A outputs.
Check one sample file path for cross-agent visibility.
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can read files and spawn subprocesses; B can read and write files. Even without explicit git access, overlapping filesystem authority on the same directory creates write-conflict risk in default multi-instance use. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF either agent writes generated artifacts into shared paths, conflicts become observable.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories for A and B.
Pause one agent while the other writes shared files.
Use read-only mounts for A where possible.
Check for duplicate filenames before running both.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a research/content-writing agent that produces citations and reports, while B is an orchestration kernel that can act on plugin outputs. If B treats A’s research as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or published outputs. Because this handoff is a default pattern in agent pipelines and no verification step is documented, high is warranted.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s report without independent verification, false facts can propagate.
IF B triggers plugins or external actions from A’s text, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Require a second-pass verification step before B acts.
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B prompts.
Limit B to summarization, not execution, on A-derived content.
Spot-check one citation chain from A before release.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles local documents, images, and multiple third-party APIs; B handles application context and plugin credentials with broad API access. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into A or B, residency and retention obligations may be implicated.
IF either agent logs prompts or context to a third-party provider, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Confirm which data classes are allowed in each agent.
Disable regulated-data inputs for one run.
Review provider retention settings for both agents.
Remove unnecessary secrets from prompts.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per agent.
